--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---

**What I built:**
- `Features/Game/CardGlyphs.swift` — four bespoke suit shapes (`HeartGlyph`, `DiamondGlyph`, `ClubGlyph`, `SpadeGlyph`) as hand-drawn `Shape`/`Path` types, not SF Symbols. Spade is derived as a vertical affine-flip of the heart path rather than hand-mirrored bezier math, so its silhouette is geometrically guaranteed consistent with the heart rather than eyeballed. `SuitGlyph.shape(for:)` type-erases via `AnyShape` (iOS 17+) since a switch can't return `some Shape` across four distinct concrete types — caught that one before it became a real compile error.
- `Features/Game/CardBackPattern.swift` — the two locked backs (`vellumSeal`, `pewterLattice`) as vector patterns (nested-ring seal vs. pewter diagonal lattice via `Canvas`), visually distinct per [REDACTED:high_entropy].
- `Features/Game/CardView.swift` — the real thing: systematic pip layout for 2-10 (counts verified against every rank), generative court-card monogram for J/Q/K, single glyph for Ace, corner index that scales with Dynamic Type via `@ScaledMetric` but clamps against physical card width so accessibility1 can't make it overlap the pip pattern, `CardVisualState` overlays (selected/legalDestination/blocked), and a base accessibility label (rank+suit+face state only — GameView still needs to append pile/position context per [REDACTED:high_entropy]'s "Seven of Hearts, tableau column 3" example, since CardView has no idea what pile it's in).

- Extended `Theme.swift` with an `Interaction` color namespace (selected/legalDestination/blocked glows) so the new overlay states don't introduce a single literal outside the theme file.
- `Interaction/DestinationAccessibilityAction.swift` and `Features/Settings/DrawModeConfirmSheet.swift` (with both declared flow tokens, `settings.drawModeConfirmSheet.confirmButton`/`cancelButton`, wired) — both zero-dependency on `GameEngine`, so safe to build now.
